our_argument_summary: WIN-025 verdict = 'Std Model Explains'. Eclipse-induced ±10 nT magnetic variations are predicted by standard Chapman-Sq ionospheric physics (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017; Kim & Chang 2018). The dome scales the station-to-station pattern via FSF = H(r)/r, but the absolute magnitude is imported from the 2017 Boulder observation. Post-EXP-624 (2026-06-16, ISS-2746 close on WIN-010), FSF is now known to be H(r)-independent — reducing algebraically to tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12 (r·tan(θ) = H(r)).

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Model publishes δZ_station = baseline × coverage × FSF. Baseline = 2017 Boulder single-station eclipse observation. FSF = H(r)/r station-to-station factor. Under V12 (r·tan(θ)=H(r)), FSF = H(r)/r = tan(θ) = tan(lat) — a pure trig identity on geographic latitude, H(r)-independent.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Chapman-Sq ionospheric framework (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017) predicts eclipse-induced ±10 nT surface variations. Chernogor & Holub 2024 attribute the observed effect to ionospheric conductivity changes, not aether. Kim & Chang 2018 39-eclipse INTERMAGNET ensemble is the standard-physics quantitative confirmation.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Sq perturbations of 5–30 nT described since 1919; quantitatively verified in Kim & Chang 2018. v31→v45 evolution log (raw-text/06-evolution.txt lines 18–21) explicitly says v31 predicted 2024 eclipse magnitudes identically across all latitudes and the FSF formula was introduced at v45 to fit the same 9-station dataset that became WIN-025.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: FSF = H(r)/r reduces algebraically to tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12 (r·tan(θ) = H(r)); the exponential H(r) is mathematically inert. Absolute magnitude baseline is imported from the 2017 Boulder observation. Neither the scaling nor the magnitude is derived from dome geometry — the scaling is a trigonometric identity on geographic latitude, and the magnitude is observation-anchored. See WIN-010 for the algebraic derivation (5 V12 mentions + 6 tan(lat) mentions in WIN-010 detail_evidence post-EXP-624).

But sentence 6 (unpatched, downstream) says 'Even after conceding FSF = H(r)/r is genuine geometry, the mechanism that produces the observed magnitudes (Chapman Sq current disruption) is the same across all three WINs...' The 'Even after conceding' clause references a concession that the patched text explicitly retracts three sentences earlier. A dome defender reading detail_verdict_text can quote sentence 6 to claim we still concede FSF is genuine geometry and treat sentence 2's V12 reduction as an internally-disputed argument. Cheap 1-sentence patch.

kernel_of_truth.description: The FSF ratio genuinely does reproduce the observed 9-station pattern to Pearson r ≈ 0.9999 (data/wins.json:025.detail_evidence). The dome DID publish an equation that generates the correct station-to-station scaling. What EXP-624 proved (see data/wins.json:010 detail_verdict_text V12/tan(lat) derivation) is that the same ratio would be generated by any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 — the ratio's H(r) dependence is algebraically inert. So the dome is 'right about the numbers' (kernel of truth) while being 'wrong about why the numbers came out that way' (H(r)-independence means the derivation is a trigonometric identity on geographic latitude, not a novel dome-geometric result).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A trigonometric identity on geographic latitude is not a scientific prediction — it is a mathematical tautology under V12. Any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 (including standard-Euclidean flat H, exponential H, polynomial H, oscillatory H) produces the same tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) ratio. The dome's specific exponential H(r) is neither necessary nor sufficient for the observed 9-station pattern — the pattern is a consequence of geographic latitude, full stop. Meanwhile the absolute magnitude (which is where a prospective test would live) is imported from the 2017 Boulder observation (data/wins.json:025.detail_evidence 'the baseline term is imported from the 2017 Boulder single-station observation'). Verdict 'Std Model Explains' correctly captures both: standard Chapman-Sq physics explains the magnitude AND the standard formula δZ ∝ f(coverage, geometry) explains the station-to-station scaling.
